about: The replay set (DIRECTION §5, F28): landed features re-run from their base commit through `plexus replay`, scored on pass rate, cost and lead time. Chosen 2026-10-23 for a spread over repos, attempts and cost; excluded: features whose checks need the live sandbox/TLS machinery, and docs- or vendoring-only work. `holdout` tasks are never tuned against: run them only to confirm a change that already won on the rest. `original` is how the feature went the first time. Every task was checked in the verifier image on 2026-10-23 (`plexus replay --check`): its acceptance fails at the base and passes where it landed. Most older plexus features can't be replayed: their tests pin heart APIs that have since changed, so plexus is under-represented until newer plexus work rotates in.

feature.title: Stdlib pulse socket reader (pulse_read.events)
feature.spec: Add src/arteries/pulse_read.py, stdlib only (http.client over AF_UNIX). Model it on heart's pulse.py socket_events: subclass http.client.HTTPConnection and override connect() to open a socket.AF_UNIX stream to the socket path. The socket path is vascular_paths.path("state", "pulse", "pulse.sock"), resolved at call time so VASCULAR_HOME set by a test applies. Public function: events(kind=None, project=None, source=None, order="asc", before=None, limit=500, timeout=2.0) -> list[dict] | None. It issues one GET /events with urlencoded query params for kind, project, source, order, before and limit, leaving out any that are None. It returns one page: the body's `events` list (pulse also returns `next` in the body, which this function ignores). Each event keeps its `seq`. A `ts` string that ends in `Z` is rewritten to end in `+00:00`. Return None on any failure: socket missing, connect refused, timeout, non-200 status, unparseable JSON, or a body without an events list. Catch Exception broadly; it must never raise. Always close the connection. Add tests/test_pulse_read.py. Each test points VASCULAR_HOME at tmp_path and starts a throwaway AF_UNIX HTTP server on a thread, bound at <tmp_path>/state/pulse/pulse.sock (http.server.HTTPServer with a socketserver.UnixStreamServer-style subclass is fine; keep the path short, and fall back to a tempfile.mkdtemp('/tmp') dir plus monkeypatched path if AF_UNIX's 108-char limit bites). Cover: the happy path (query string carries kind/source/order/before/limit, seq kept, Z converted), no socket -> None, 500 status -> None, bad JSON -> None, and a server that never replies with timeout=0.2 -> None. No real pulse, nothing written into the checkout.

feature.title: Episodes and roles open spans; in-episode events parent to the episode span
feature.spec: In src/heart/episode.py, put the trace and span handling in `run_episode`, the public wrapper. `_run_episode` emits episode.started and episode.finished, but episode.failed is emitted by run_episode's `except`, so the wrapper is the only place that covers all three. Put it around the try/except that calls `_run_episode`, before or after the routing.pick call (route.decided may go either way). Steps: (1) Save prev_trace = os.environ.get("PULSE_TRACE_ID") and prev_parent = os.environ.get("PULSE_PARENT_SPAN"). If prev_trace is unset or empty, set os.environ["PULSE_TRACE_ID"] = os.urandom(16).hex(). (2) Generate ep_span = pulse_emit.new_span() (import pulse_emit from the package) and pass it into `_run_episode` with a new keyword parameter `ep_span: str | None = None`. The finally restores PULSE_PARENT_SPAN to its value from before (pop it if it was unset), so episode.finished, emitted with span_id=ep_span, keeps the caller's parent. (4) In run_episode, episode.failed gets span_id=ep_span. After the try/except, in a finally, restore PULSE_TRACE_ID (pop if prev_trace was unset or empty, else restore it) and restore PULSE_PARENT_SPAN to prev_parent (pop if None), as a backstop. (5) Roles: at the pipeline call site (role.started, around line 796), make role_span = pulse_emit.new_span(), emit role.started with span_id=role_span, and pass span_id=role_span to `_agent_turn`. Add `span_id: str | None = None` as the last parameter of `_agent_turn`. If it is None, generate one with pulse_emit.new_span(), so fix-loop and review turns get a span that only has a finish. Emit role.finished with span_id=span_id. parent_span_id stays implicit everywhere: pulse_emit reads it from $PULSE_PARENT_SPAN, which is ep_span inside the episode. Add a `ponytail:` comment where the env is set. It must say: process-global env, safe because one episode runs per process in this path; run_candidates' thread pool (n>1) shares os.environ and can mis-parent concurrent candidates' events; contextvars passed to events.emit are the upgrade if episodes ever run concurrently in one process. Every role.started has a role.finished with the same span_id, and both have parent_span_id == S. Every other line except episode.* and route.decided has parent_span_id == S. Afterwards PULSE_TRACE_ID and PULSE_PARENT_SPAN are not in os.environ. (b) `test_trace_span_episode_under_parent`: set PULSE_TRACE_ID=t-outer and PULSE_PARENT_SPAN=p-outer first. feature.title: routing.pick() considers only models named in models.json route_models
feature.spec:
Add an optional top-level `route_models` list of model nicknames to models.json, next to `review_models`. Routing reads it; review does not. All changes live in src/heart/routing.py.

1. Add `route_models() -> list[str]` in routing.py. It returns `load_models_json().get("route_models")` when that value is a non-empty list of strings, and `[]` otherwise (absent, empty, or the wrong type). It must never raise.

2. Give `pick()` a new keyword parameter `route_models: list[str] | None = None`. When it is None, pick reads `route_models()` itself. Callers that pass their own `manifest=` (orchestrate.py, episode.py) therefore obey the operator's list without changes, and so do `heart` and plexus's `auto`, which both go through pick. Passing `route_models=[]` explicitly turns the filter off. Do not change any caller. Do not touch review.py, review_models or review_agent.

3. Inside pick, after the `if not manifest:` branch, resolve the allowlist against the manifest. Any name not in `manifest` gets a one-line warning on stderr, `heart: route_models: unknown model '<name>' ignored`, and is then dropped. If no known names remain, the allowlist counts as absent and behaviour is exactly what it is today. Otherwise, during the existing filter loop, every manifest entry outside the allowlist is skipped before any other check, with `filtered.append(f"{name}:not in route_models")`. That puts the entry in route.decided's `filtered` the same way the other filters do. Allowlisted entries run through the existing unavailable/context/difficulty filters and scoring unchanged, and `_best` still breaks ties toward the cheapest among them.

4. Fallback when an allowlist is active and `scored` ends up empty: never pick a model outside the allowlist. Take the allowlisted entries that are available (availability is physical, so keep honouring `available`) and ignore the context and difficulty filters. Choose by highest `max_difficulty` rank, then largest `context`. Return it through `decided(...)` with effort "high", a reason starting `no model cleared constraints (` like today's fallback, and the full `filtered` list. With an allowlist active, this replaces the current `raise ValueError("no available model satisfies context constraints...")`. Raise that ValueError only if no allowlisted entry is available. Without an allowlist, the existing fallback and raise stay byte-for-byte the same.

5. Do not read or write ~/.vascular/config/heart/models.json in code or tests. The operator sets route_models there by hand.

6. New file tests/test_route_models.py, pytest style. A module-level autouse fixture sets EVENT_JOURNAL_DIR and VASCULAR_HOME to tmp_path via monkeypatch, so route.decided events and config reads never touch the real ~/.vascular. The manifest stub, in the same raw shape tests/test_route_orchestrate.py uses: opus (agent "claude", cost 3.0), sol (agent "api:sol", cost 2.5), sonnet (agent "api:sonnet", cost 0.5), terra (agent "api:terra", cost 0.3). All four get skills {"coding": 0.9}, context 200_000 and max_difficulty "hard". Demands come from `routing.demand(TaskSpec(task_id="t", repo_path=".", base_commit="x", prompt="add a function", skills=["coding"], difficulty=...))`. To read `filtered`, monkeypatch `routing.emit` to capture kwargs. Tests:
(a) route_models=["opus","sol"] at easy, medium and hard difficulty: the choice's name is never sonnet or terra, and the captured `filtered` contains "sonnet:not in route_models" and "terra:not in route_models".
(b) route_models=[] (and, separately, None with no models.json under VASCULAR_HOME): picks terra, the cheapest on a tie, as today.
(c) route_models=["opus","nope"]: picks opus, does not raise, and capsys shows a warning mentioning 'nope' on stderr. route_models=["nope"] alone behaves like (b) and picks terra.
(d) A manifest where opus and sol have context 32_000 and the demand has min_context=100_000, with route_models=["opus","sol"]: returns opus or sol, never sonnet or terra, and the reason starts with "no model cleared constraints". Also the difficulty variant: opus and sol at max_difficulty "easy" with a hard demand also returns one of opus or sol.
(e) With no route_models argument, write `{"models": {...stub...}, "route_models": ["opus","sol"]}` to the models.json path under the tmp VASCULAR_HOME (find the path via `heart.agents_api.models_json_path()`), then call `pick(want, manifest=routing.load_manifest())`: the result is opus or sol. This proves the config is read on the caller's manifest path.

feature.title: Count every started attempt in insights/report, with per-task outcomes and spend
feature.spec:
In src/plexus/observe.py, add attempt_outcomes(recs: list[dict]) -> list[dict]. It returns one dict per feature.started record: {goal_id, task, feature_id, attempt, outcome, cost_usd, tokens_in, tokens_out}. task is the feature_id prefix before ':' or '(none)' when there is no ':'. The attempt is settled by the first of these records for the same (goal_id, feature_id) after its feature.started and before that feature's next feature.started. feature.landed gives landed. feature.failed gives failed. For escalation.raised, the outcome follows reason_class: held_for_review or held_stale give held, scope_violation gives scope, and any other reason_class gives blocked. If nothing settles it, the outcome is crashed. A later feature.landed with from_held=<episode> relabels the held attempt whose escalation named that episode in episode_ids as landed, without adding cost. cost_usd/tokens come from the settling record; legacy held escalations without cost_usd fall back to held_cost; if neither exists, the value is None (unknown). feature.spec:

Returns the lines and the new checkpoint of every file it touched. `Line { pub file: String /* day file name only */, pub offset: u64 /* byte offset of first byte */, pub bytes: Vec<u8> /* without the '\n' */ }`.
- `pulse::ingest::ingest(file: &str, offset: u64, bytes: &[u8]) -> Ingested` with `enum Ingested { Event(EventRow), Quarantine(QuarantineRow) }`. `EventRow.context: Option<ContextRow>` is Some for a `context.started` line carrying a context_id. - `pulse::store::{Store, Batch, StoreError, MemoryStore}`: `trait Store { fn checkpoints(&mut self) -> Result<HashMap<String,u64>, StoreError>; fn commit(&mut self, batch: &Batch) -> Result<(), StoreError>; }`, `Batch { events: Vec<EventRow>, contexts: Vec<ContextRow>, quarantine: Vec<QuarantineRow>, checkpoints: HashMap<String,u64> }` (derives Default), commit all-or-nothing, duplicate ids / (file, offset) are silent no-ops. `StoreError(pub String)` implements `From<std::io::Error>`. `MemoryStore` has public fields `events`, `contexts`, `quarantine`, `checkpoints` and `fail_next: usize` (while > 0, each commit decrements it, stores nothing and errors).

- `#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default, PartialEq, Eq)] pub struct PassStats { pub events: usize, pub quarantined: usize, pub contexts: usize }` — counts the rows in the batches this pass committed successfully (rows the store dropped as duplicates still count; nothing from a failed commit counts).
- `pub fn pass(store: &mut impl Store, journal_dir: &Path, batch_lines: usize) -> Result<PassStats, StoreError>`: read checkpoints from the store once; loop: `spool::read_new(journal_dir, &checkpoints, batch_lines)?`; if no lines, stop and return the stats; otherwise ingest each line into a Batch (event rows to `events`, and if `row.context` is Some, a clone of it to `contexts`; quarantine rows to `quarantine`), set `batch.checkpoints` to the map read_new returned, `store.commit(&batch)?` — on error return it immediately (the checkpoint did not move, so the next pass re-reads the same lines) — then merge the new checkpoints into the local map (`extend`), add to the stats, and repeat. A bad line never stops the pass. Guard `batch_lines == 0` so it doesn't loop forever (read_new returns nothing, so the loop just ends).

Add `tests/collect.rs` using MemoryStore over a fresh scratch dir under `std::env::temp_dir()` (unique per test: test name + process id + nanos; never write into the checkout), day files named like `20261013.ndjson`, synthetic lines only, e.g. `{"ts":"2026-06-15T08:30:00Z","source":"heart","kind":"x.y","id":"<uuid>"}`. 1. every line lands once: N lines across two day files → store.events has N rows with N distinct ids and PassStats.events == N; checkpoints equal each file's length.
2. running pass twice adds nothing: second pass returns PassStats::default() and the store is unchanged.
3. two identical legacy lines (no `id`) both survive as two events with different ids.
4. a failed commit loses nothing: set `fail_next = 1`, pass returns Err, store holds no rows and no checkpoints; the next pass delivers every line exactly once. feature.title: Parse and validate an event line against contract/envelope.json, with synthetic example files
feature.spec:
Pulse is a Rust crate (edition 2024, toolchain 1.99.0). Implement P1's envelope validator in src/envelope.rs, export it from src/lib.rs with `pub mod envelope;` (keep the existing doc comment), and add synthetic example files plus the integration test tests/envelope.rs.

HARD CONSTRAINTS:
- Dependencies: only serde and serde_json, already in Cargo.toml and baked into the verifier image. No other crate, not even a dev-dependency: the verifier has no network. If something seems to need one, stop and ask (PLEXUS_BLOCKED). Do not touch Cargo.toml or Cargo.lock.
- Do not edit contract/envelope.json or contract/observed.json. They are inputs.
- This repo is public: every example line is synthetic. Use made-up ids, paths like /work/demo, and short invented text. Never copy anything that looks like a real journal line.
- Always `cargo ... --locked`. Tests write nothing into the checkout, run no git, and use no network. Read files relative to env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR").

INPUT: contract/envelope.json has a `required` map (field name -> type name), an `optional` map (same shape), a `types` map describing each type name, and a `rules` list. Currently required = ts:timestamp, source:name, kind:kind; optional includes id:uuid, schema_version:integer, emitter_seq:integer, duration_ms:number, origin:origin, payload:object and many `string` fields. Read the file itself for the full list.

REQUIREMENTS:
1. envelope.json drives the validator: embed it with `include_str!("../contract/envelope.json")` and read its `required` and `optional` maps at runtime, parsed once (std::sync::OnceLock). Adding a field to the JSON must change behaviour with no Rust edit. Only the type names (`string`, `integer`, `number`, `object`, `uuid`, `timestamp`, `name`, `kind`, `origin`) are implemented in code. An unknown type name in the JSON must panic during that one-time parse with a message naming the type, so any test that calls parse_line fails (an unknown type is a test failure, not a silent pass).
2. `pub fn parse_line(line: &str) -> Result<Event, EnvelopeError>`. `pub struct Event { pub ts: String, pub source: String, pub kind: String, pub fields: serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value> }` where `fields` holds ALL top-level fields of the line exactly as parsed (ts/source/kind and unknown fields included: skip and retain). Derive Debug and Clone on Event.
3. Implement each rule in envelope.json's `rules` list:
   - A line that is not valid JSON -> not_json. Valid JSON that is not an object -> not_object.
   - A required field that is missing or null -> missing_field.
   - An optional field that is null counts as absent (accepted, no check).
   - Any present field of the wrong JSON type -> wrong_type. For uuid/timestamp/name/kind/origin a non-string value is wrong_type; a string in the wrong format gives the specific code (bad_uuid, bad_timestamp, bad_name, bad_kind, bad_origin).
   - `integer`: serde_json `as_u64()` is Some (so negatives and 3.5 are wrong_type). `number`: a JSON number >= 0, else wrong_type. `object`: JSON object. `string`: JSON string.
   - Unknown top-level fields are kept, never rejected. Unknown kinds are accepted (no catalog check here). Absent origin means unknown; nothing to store (downstream exports decide).
   Check fields in order: required map then optional map, return the first error.
4. Check formats by hand (no regex crate):
   - timestamp: `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS`, an optional `.` plus 1-9 digits, then `Z` or `+hh:mm`/`-hh:mm`. `T` and `Z` uppercase only. Month 01-12, day 01-31, hour 00-23, minute 00-59, second 00-59, offset hh 00-23 and mm 00-59. Nothing else may follow.
   - uuid: 8-4-4-4-12 hex digits (either case) separated by `-`, 36 chars total.
   - name: matches ^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*$
   - kind: matches ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*(\.[a-z][a-z0-9_]*)+$ (at least two dot-separated segments, each starting with a lowercase letter).
   - origin: exactly "operator", "agent" or "external".

5. `pub enum EnvelopeError` (derive Debug, Clone, PartialEq) with variants carrying the field name where one applies, a stable `pub fn code(&self) -> &'static str` returning exactly one of: `not_json`, `not_object`, `missing_field`, `wrong_type`, `bad_timestamp`, `bad_uuid`, `bad_name`, `bad_kind`, `bad_origin`. Implement Display so the message names the field (e.g. `wrong_type: field "emitter_seq" ...`; for not_json/not_object say `line`). Implement std::error::Error.
6. Example files (synthetic only), newline-delimited JSON, one event per line:
   - contract/examples/valid/*.ndjson, a few files (e.g. basic.ndjson, optional.ndjson, edge.ndjson), at least 20 non-empty lines total. Cover every optional field in envelope.json at least once, an unknown top-level field, an unknown kind, a null payload, origin "operator", "agent" and "external", ts with `Z`, with `+00:00` and with fractional seconds.
   - Every valid line's (source, kind) pair must either appear as a pair in contract/observed.json, or its kind must start with `example.` (use `example.` kinds for deliberately unknown kinds, e.g. `example.widget.spun`).
   - contract/examples/invalid/<code>.ndjson for each of the nine codes (e.g. invalid/bad_kind.ndjson), at least 2 non-empty lines each, every line failing with exactly that file's code.
7. tests/envelope.rs (integration test, uses `pulse::envelope`):
   - Reads every contract/examples/valid/*.ndjson; each non-empty line must parse (failure message names file and line number).
   - Every valid line's (source, kind) is in contract/observed.json (parse it with serde_json: `{"kinds": [{"source", "kind", ...}]}`) or the kind starts with `example.`.
   - Reads every contract/examples/invalid/<code>.ndjson; each non-empty line must fail with `code()` equal to the file stem. Asserts at least one invalid file exists per code (all nine) and that no invalid file has a stem outside the nine.
   - Unit-level cases: unknown field retained in `fields`; unknown kind accepted; null optional (e.g. payload: null, emitter_seq: null) accepted; `Z` and `+00:00` both accepted; fractional seconds accepted; `2026-13-01T00:00:00Z` rejected with bad_timestamp; missing ts gives missing_field; negative emitter_seq gives wrong_type; Display of an error contains the field name.
8. Run `cargo fmt` and fix every clippy warning.

feature.title: src/http.rs: minimal HTTP/1.1 GET over a Unix socket (server parse/respond + client get)
feature.spec:
Add a new module `src/http.rs` and declare it in `src/lib.rs` as `pub mod http;`. Insert it in alphabetical order among the existing `pub mod` lines (artifacts, catalog, collect, envelope, ingest, paths, pg, spool, store), so it goes between `envelope` and `ingest`. Use std only. Cargo.toml must not change, and no dependency may be added (the verifier has no network). Do not touch contract/ or sql/. This is the wire layer for pulse's query API (PLAN.md P4). The API is plain HTTP/1.1, GET only, one request per connection, served one connection at a time on a Unix socket. Routing, handlers and the CLI belong to later tasks; do not build them here. Give the module a short `//!` doc comment in the same style as the other modules.

Public surface:

1. `pub struct Request { pub path: String, pub query: Vec<(String, String)> }`. Derive Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq. `path` is the request target before any `?`, percent-decoded. A `+` in the path stays a literal `+`. `query` holds the pairs after `?` in their original order. Split on `&` and skip empty pieces. Split each piece on its first `=`; a piece without `=` becomes (key, ""). Keys and values are percent-decoded, and `+` decodes to a space. After percent-decoding, the bytes must be valid UTF-8. A repeated key keeps every occurrence.

2. `pub enum HttpError { Method(String), BadRequest(String) }`. Derive Debug. `Method` carries the refused method name. Implement `std::fmt::Display` with a human-readable message, e.g. `method not allowed: POST` or `bad request: <reason>`. Also implement `std::error::Error`.

3. `pub fn read_request(r: &mut impl BufRead) -> Result<Request, HttpError>`:
   - Read the request line, then header lines, up to and including the first empty line. A line may end in CRLF or a bare LF; strip the trailing `\r` if present.
   - The whole header section (request line plus headers plus terminators) is capped at 16 KiB (16384 bytes). Enforce the cap while reading, e.g. via `Read::take` on a running budget, so an endless line never buffers unbounded memory. Going over the cap returns `HttpError::BadRequest`.
   - EOF before the blank line returns `BadRequest`, as does an I/O error (put the error text in the message). The same goes for a request line that is not exactly three space-separated parts `METHOD TARGET VERSION`, a VERSION that doesn't start with `HTTP/1.`, a target that doesn't start with `/`, and non-UTF-8 header bytes.
   - A well-formed request line whose method is not exactly `GET` returns `HttpError::Method(method)`.
   - Invalid percent-encoding in the path or query returns `BadRequest`. That covers `%` not followed by two hex digits (e.g. `%zz`, or a trailing `%` or `%4`) and decoded bytes that aren't valid UTF-8.
   - Ignore header contents, and never read a body.

4. `pub fn write_response(w: &mut impl Write, status: u16, content_type: &str, body: &[u8]) -> std::io::Result<()>`. Write exactly `HTTP/1.1 {status} {reason}\r\nContent-Type: {content_type}\r\nContent-Length: {body.len()}\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n`, then the body bytes, then flush. Reasons: 200 `OK`, 400 `Bad Request`, 404 `Not Found`, 405 `Method Not Allowed`, 500 `Internal Server Error`, 503 `Service Unavailable`. Any other status gets `Unknown`.

5. `pub fn encode(s: &str) -> String` percent-encodes a query value for callers building URLs. Pass the unreserved bytes `A-Z a-z 0-9 - . _ ~` through unchanged and write every other byte of the UTF-8 encoding as `%XX` with uppercase hex. A space becomes `%20`. The result must round-trip through read_request's query decoding.

6. `pub fn get(socket: &std::path::Path, path_and_query: &str) -> std::io::Result<(u16, Vec<u8>)>`. This is the client side.
   - Connect a `std::os::unix::net::UnixStream` to `socket` and write `GET {path_and_query} HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: pulse\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n`.
   - Wrap the stream in a BufReader. Read the status line `HTTP/1.x <code> <reason>` and parse the code as u16, then read header lines (CRLF or bare LF) up to the blank line. Match `Content-Length` case-insensitively and trim its value.
   - With a Content-Length, read exactly that many bytes (read_exact). Without one, read to EOF.
   - A malformed status line or an unparsable Content-Length returns `io::Error` of kind `InvalidData`.
   - Return (status, body). The body is raw bytes and may contain any byte values.

Tests: create `tests/http.rs` (integration tests using `pulse::http::*`; use only std). Cover:
   (a) Parse `GET /events?kind=a.b&project=my%20proj&x=1+2 HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: pulse\r\n\r\n` from a `std::io::Cursor`. Expect path `/events` and query `[("kind","a.b"),("project","my proj"),("x","1 2")]`.
   (b) A bare-LF request (`GET /health HTTP/1.1\nHost: x\n\n`) parses to path `/health` with an empty query.
   (c) `POST /events HTTP/1.1\r\n\r\n` returns `Err(HttpError::Method(m))` with m == "POST".
   (d) A request whose header section exceeds 16 KiB is refused with `BadRequest`. Use, e.g., one header line of 17000 `a` characters followed by a blank line.
   (e) `GET /events?kind=%zz HTTP/1.1\r\n\r\n` returns `BadRequest`, and so does a trailing `%4`.
   (f) The exact bytes of `write_response` for status 200, content type `application/json` and body `{}`: `HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nContent-Type: application/json\r\nContent-Length: 2\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n{}`. Also check that 404 yields the `HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found\r\n` prefix.
   (g) `encode("my proj/a&b=c+é")` is `my%20proj%2Fa%26b%3Dc%2B%C3%A9`, and it round-trips through read_request as a query value.
   (h) Round trip. Bind a `std::os::unix::net::UnixListener` at a short unique path under `std::env::temp_dir()`, e.g. `pulse-http-{pid}-{n}.sock`, keeping the path under 100 bytes. Remove any stale file first. Spawn a thread that accepts one connection, wraps it in a BufReader, calls read_request, and answers with write_response. Make the status and body depend on the parsed request: for example, path `/bin` answers 200 with body bytes `[0u8, 127, 128, 200, 255]` plus the decoded `x` query value. Call `get(&sock, "/bin?x=" + &encode("a b"))` and assert the status and exact body bytes. Do a second connection or listener that answers 404, and assert `get` returns 404. Join the thread and remove the socket file afterwards.
   Tests must never write into the checkout or run git, and need no network or Postgres.

Acceptance runs from the repository root: `cargo fmt --check && cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings && cargo test --locked --test http`. The existing suite must keep passing too.

feature.title: src/spool.rs: read complete lines from YYYYMMDD.ndjson day files from per-file checkpoints
feature.spec:
Add a new module `src/spool.rs` and register it with `pub mod spool;` in src/lib.rs, next to the existing `pub mod catalog; pub mod envelope; pub mod paths;`. Use the standard library only. Do not add dependencies; Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock stay as they are. Do not edit contract/ or sql/. Edition 2024, toolchain 1.99.0.

Context: this is the reader for the pulse collector (PLAN.md P3). Other processes append NDJSON events to day files in the journal directory, the one `paths::journal_dir` returns. This module takes a directory as `&Path` and does not call `paths`. The collector tails those files from per-file byte checkpoints.

Public API:
```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Line {
    pub file: String,   // day file name only, e.g. "20261013.ndjson"
    pub offset: u64,    // byte offset of the line's first byte in that file
    pub bytes: Vec<u8>, // the line without its trailing '\n'
}

pub fn read_new(
    dir: &Path,
    checkpoints: &HashMap<String, u64>,
    max_lines: usize,
) -> std::io::Result<(Vec<Line>, HashMap<String, u64>)>
```

Behaviour:
- Day files are regular files directly in `dir` whose name is exactly 8 ASCII digits followed by `.ndjson` (`YYYYMMDD.ndjson`). Skip every other name, and skip every subdirectory even if its name matches. `incoming/` belongs to arteries and is already folded into the day files. Do not recurse.
- Process day files in ascending name order (sort the names).
- For each file, start at `checkpoints.get(name)`, or 0 if the name is absent. If the checkpoint is larger than the file's current length (the file was truncated or replaced), restart that file at 0.
- Read from the start position only through the last `\n` in the file. Bytes after the last newline are a partial line that another process is still appending. Never return them and never advance the checkpoint past them; the next call picks them up once completed.
- Split the complete region on `\n`. Each non-empty line becomes a `Line` with `offset` = the absolute byte offset of its first byte, and `bytes` holding the content without the newline. Lines are raw bytes: do not decode UTF-8 or strip `\r`. Empty lines (a bare `\n`) are not returned, but they still advance the checkpoint.
- Stop once `max_lines` lines have been returned in total across all files. `max_lines == 0` returns no lines and an empty map.
- The returned map holds an entry for every file touched: each file that had at least one complete line, empty ones included, consumed in this call. Its value is the byte position just past the `\n` of the last line consumed. If the limit stops a file partway, the value is just past the last line returned, so the next call resumes exactly there. Files with nothing new are left out of the returned map. One exception: a file that restarted at 0 because of truncation and has no complete line yet should get an entry of 0, so the caller drops its stale checkpoint. The caller merges the returned map into its own; you don't need to echo untouched entries.
- A missing `dir` is an io error; return it. Errors reading a file are returned with `?`.
- Simplest acceptable implementation: for each file, open it, seek to the start position, read the rest into a Vec with `read_to_end`, find the last `\n` with `rposition`, and split. ponytail: whole-tail read; switch to a bounded read if day files get large.

Tests: create `tests/spool.rs`, an integration test using `pulse::spool::{read_new, Line}`. Check the crate name in Cargo.toml and use whatever it is. Each test makes its own scratch directory under `std::env::temp_dir()`, with a unique name such as the test name plus process id plus nanos. Never write into the checkout. Remove the directory at the end where practical. No git, no network. All data synthetic (e.g. `{"n":1}`). Required tests:
1. Partial last line: the file holds `a\nb\npart` with no trailing newline. The first call returns `a` and `b` only, and the checkpoint is 4. Append `ial\n`. The next call, with the merged checkpoints, returns exactly one line `partial` at offset 4.
2. Resume: 5 lines; call with max_lines=2, then again with the returned checkpoints. Lines are returned in order with no duplicates and no gaps, and a final call returns nothing.
3. `max_lines` across files: `20261012.ndjson` has 2 lines and `20261013.ndjson` has 3. max_lines=3 returns both lines of the first file plus the first line of the second, and the checkpoints for both are correct. The next call returns the remaining 2.
4. Ignored entries: complete lines in `notes.txt`, `2026101.ndjson`, `20261013.ndjson.tmp`, a subdirectory `incoming/` holding `20261013.ndjson`, and a subdirectory named `20261014.ndjson`. Only lines from the real top-level day file come back, and the returned map holds only that file name.
5. Exact offsets with multi-byte UTF-8: lines such as `{"m":"héllo"}`, `{"m":"日本語"}`, `{"m":"🦀"}`, plus an empty line in between. For every returned Line, check that `offset == 0` or `content[offset-1] == b'\n'`, that `content[offset..offset+bytes.len()] == bytes[..]`, and that `content[offset+bytes.len()] == b'\n'`. Check that the empty line is not returned and the checkpoint equals the file length.
6. Truncation: read a 3-line file to its end, then rewrite it shorter with a single different line. The next call, given the old checkpoint, returns that line at offset 0.

Acceptance: `cargo fmt --check && cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings && cargo test --locked --test spool`, run from the repository root.
